full_judgment:
Mohi Uddin Shamim, J: This Rule was issued on an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure at the instance of the accused-petitioners Gazi Muhammad Rafiqullah Nesari and three others, calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the proceeding of Special Case No. 2 of 2013 arising out of Nalchity Police Station Case No. 19 dated 20-3-2008 corresponding to GR No. 53 of 2008 (Nal) under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code along with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, now pending in the Court of Special Judge, Second Court, Jhalakati, should not be quashed and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Facts necessary for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that Sekandar Hayet Rizbi, Upazilla Nirbahi Officer (UNO), Nalchity, Jhalakathi lodged a first information report (FIR) with Nalchity Police Station alleging, inter-alia, that the accused-petitioner No. 1 as Superintendent of local Kulkathi Shahidia Dakhil Madrasha drew up an amount of Taka 1,25,000 through a cheque bearing No. 5163643 dated 9-12-2007 which was granted by the Government for repairing the damage caused to the aforesaid Madrasha due to devastating cyclone, namely, Sidr. The accused-petitioner No. 1 did not spend the whole money for repairing the aforesaid Madrasha. He was asked by the UNO to deposit the unspent money amounting to Taka 51,589 to the Government Treasury, but he did not do so. On the basis of the aforesaid FIR, Nalchity Police Station Case No. 19 dated 20-3-2008 under section 409 of the Penal Code was initialed against the accused-petitioner No. 1. 

 3. Thereafter, the case was sent to the Anti-Corruption Commission (shortly, the ACC) for investigation. Whereupon, a Deputy Assistant Director of the ACC, Combined District Office, Barisal was entrusted with the investigation of the case. After thorough investigation, the investigating officer submitted charge-sheet being No. 29 dated 04-3-2012 under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code along with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 against the present accused-petitioners. 

 4. Thereafter, the case record was transmitted to the 2nd Court of Special Judge, Jhalakati for trial wherein, the case was numbered as Special Case No. 02 of 2013. 

 5. The case was fixed for framing of charge on 20-6-2013 and the accused-petitioners filed an application under section 241A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for discharging them from the case. Upon hearing the parties, the learned Judge rejected the aforesaid application and framed charge against the accused-petitioners under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code along with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. 

 6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the impugned proceeding, the petitioners preferred the instant miscellaneous case under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the Rule. 

 7. Mr Md Jahirul Islam Suman, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, takes us through the miscellaneous application, the FIR, the charge-sheet, other connected materials on record and submits that after initiation of the instant case, the petitioners filed application before the Truth and Accountability Commission for mercy by admitting their guilt and upon hearing, the Truth Commission granted mercy and directed them to deposit the mis-appropriated money to the Government Treasury. Accordingly, the petitioners complied with the direction of the Commission by depositing the respective amount of mis-appropriated money. By mentioning the provisions of section 403 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, section 26 of the General Clauses Act and article 35 of the Constitution, he submits that under the above provisions of law, no person can be tried again for the self-same offence wherein he had already been tried and acquitted. He further submits that under section 20 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004, no Gazette was published entrusting any competent officer to investigate into the case and under rule 10 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007, the investigation of any case should have been concluded within sixty days from the date of taking charge for investigation, but in the instant case, the charge-sheet was submitted on 4-3-2012 i.e. after more than four years from the date of institution of the case. Therefore, there are serious legal defects in the instant case and the benefit of which must go in favour of the accused. He finally submits that the instant proceeding is nothing but a vexatious one and to prevent the abuse of the process of the Court, the proceeding is liable to be quashed and the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 8. Mr AKM Alamgir Parvez Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party No. 2, the ACC, contends that the materials available on record disclose a prima-facie case against the accused-petitioners under the offence charged. He next contends that the grounds taken by the petitioners for quashment of the proceeding relating to granting mercy to the petitioners by the Truth and Accountability Commission, deposit of misappropriated money by them pursuant to the direction of the Commission, the initiation and investigation of the case beyond the statutory period of law all these are the disputed question of facts, which cannot be decided under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Rather, those are to be decided by the Trial Court on the basis of evidence adduced by the prosecution. He further contends that the grounds as embodied in the miscellaneous petition are the defence plea of the accused-petitioners, which cannot be decided under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure without examining the evidence. He also contends that the Trial Court will consider the case and the defence case of the parties on the basis of evidence to be adduced by the parties and if the petitioners are found to be not guilty of the offence charged, definitely, they would be acquitted. He finally contends that in consideration of the materials on record, the impugned proceeding does not call for any interference by this Court under its inherent jurisdiction under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 9. Mr AKM Amin Uddin, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing with Ms. Mehjabin Rabbani (Deepa) and Ms. Anna Khanom (Koli), the learned Assistant Attorney-Generals, on behalf of the State, submits that the accused-petitioners are apparently involved in misappropriating the public money granted by the Government and they should be tried for the offence charged. He next submits that the every aspect of the allegation against the accused-petitioners is to be proved through trial and, as such, the accused-petitioners have no other option but to face the trial. He further submits that there is no legal ground for quashing the proceeding. Rather, there is neither any preposterousness nor any legal bar nor any allegation in the FIR which does not constitute any offence against the accused-petitioners. Therefore, considering the factual and legal aspects of the case and perusing the materials on record, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 10. We have heard the learned Advocate for the petitioners, the learned Advocate for the ACC as well as the learned Deputy Attorney-General for the State. We have also perused the miscellaneous application, the counter-affidavit filed by the opposite-party No. 2 and the other connected materials available on record. 

 11. On perusing the miscellaneous application, it is evident that the sheet anchor of the petitioners in the instant case is the order of the Truth and Accountability Commission, wherein, the accused-petitioners have allegedly been granted mercy earlier for the alleged offence and it is their claim that pursuant to the direction of the Commission, they deposited the respective amount of misappropriated money in the Government Treasury. It be noted here that no such order of the Truth Commission has been annexed with the miscellaneous application. Moreover, had it been annexed with the miscellaneous application, it would have not been possible by us to examine the veracity of the aforesaid order of the Truth Commission under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. It is the Trial Court which is capable to test and examine the same during trial. 

 12. From the plain reading of the FIR as well as the charge-sheet (Annexures-A and C to the miscellaneous application), prima-facie, it appears to us that the elements of the offence under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code along with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 are available there in the instant case and accordingly, charge was also framed against the accused-petitioners under the aforesaid sections of the laws. The grounds for quashment of the impugned proceeding as embodied in the miscellaneous petition are disputed question of facts. In a proceeding under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the High Court Division has little scope to scrutinize the truth or otherwise of any fact or the evidence which may be used as defence materials in a criminal proceeding. Therefore, the impugned proceeding does not warrant any interference by this Court exercising its inherent power under section 561A of the Code. Therefore, there is no scope for us for interference with the impugned proceeding under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure by exercising inherent jurisdiction. 

 13. Moreover, by taking some grounds in the miscellaneous application, the petitioners tried to show that there are some legal defects that there was no publication of Gazette entrusting an officer to investigate into the case under section 20 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 as well as the investigating officer could not conclude the investigation of the case within the statutory period of law under rule 10 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Rules, 2007 and, as such, the proceeding is liable to be quashed. Though the ground relating to time limit for completion of investigation appears to be a legal ground, but, admittedly, there is no such time limitation for completion of any investigation under the aforesaid Rules. Rather, it is the section 20Ka of the Anit-Corruption Commission Act, 2004, wherein some periods of time have been stipulated to complete the investigation. But there is no such default clause in the above Act that if the investigation is not completed within the stipulated periods of time, then what is to be done.
